## Load data from step 2

```{r}
load(here("data", "02_cancer_clean.RData"))
```


## Top mutated genes

For each gene, count how many different samples carry at least one mutation
in it. A sample with several mutations in the same gene counts only once.

```{r}
n_samples = nrow(clinical)

gene_mutation_freq <- mutations |>
  distinct(patient_id,
           tumor_barcode,
           hugo_symbol) |>
  count(hugo_symbol,
        name = "n_mutated_samples") |>
  mutate(pct_mutated_samples = n_mutated_samples / n_samples * 100,
         gene_rank = row_number(desc(n_mutated_samples))) |>
  arrange(gene_rank)
```

Plot the mutation frequency distribution with gene rank, to choose how many
genes to keep for our further analysis.

```{r}
gene_mutation_freq |>
  filter(gene_rank <= 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gene_rank,
             y = pct_mutated_samples)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 20,
             linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Gene rank",
       y = "Samples with a mutation (in %)",
       title = "Mutation frequency of the 100 most mutated genes")
```

The curves starts to flatten and decrease very slowly after ran 20, so we have
chosen to focus on the top 20 genes only.

```{r}
n_top_genes <- 20

top_genes <- gene_mutation_freq |>
  filter(gene_rank <= n_top_genes) |>
  pull(hugo_symbol)

top_genes
```

Add the mutation length and a flag for our list of "top genes".

```{r}
mutation_augment <- mutations |>
  mutate(length_mutation = end_position - start_position,
         is_top_gene = hugo_symbol %in% top_genes)
```

## Gene Matrix of top 20 genes

Reshape the mutation_augment list from a long format into a wide table so that
each row represents one unique tumor sample and each of the 20 genes becomes
its own dedicated column.

```{r}
gene_matrix <- mutation_augment |>
  filter(hugo_symbol %in% top_genes) |>
  count(patient_id, tumor_barcode, hugo_symbol, name = "n_mut") |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = hugo_symbol,
    values_from = n_mut,
    names_prefix = "num_mut_",
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

## New table named clinical_augment (gene_matrix merged onto clinical)

Keep the samples with no mutation rows and give them 0

```{r}
clinical_augment <- clinical |>
  left_join(
    gene_matrix,
    by = c("patient_id" = "patient_id", "sample_barcode" = "tumor_barcode")
  ) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("num_mut_"), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
```

Calculate total number of mutations per sample and number of distinct mutated genes
from mutation_augment and join them onto clinical_augment

```{r}
sample_mut_summary <- mutation_augment |>
  group_by(patient_id, tumor_barcode) |>
  summarise(
    total_mutations = n(),
    n_distinct_genes = n_distinct(hugo_symbol),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

clinical_augment <- clinical_augment |>
  left_join(
    sample_mut_summary,
    by = c("patient_id" = "patient_id", "sample_barcode" = "tumor_barcode")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    total_mutations = replace_na(total_mutations, 0),
    n_distinct_genes = replace_na(n_distinct_genes, 0)
  )
```


## Save the augmented datasets and top 20 gene list to an .RData file

```{r}
save(clinical_augment,
     mutation_augment,
     top_genes,
     file = here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))
```
